The same estimates follow from a derivation in vector notation,
which treats $(\intcoef, \coef{x})$ as a single vector
instead of differentiating with respect to each component separately.

Use the coefficient vector $\vcoef = \tp{\paren{\intcoef, \coef{x}}}$
from @exm-normal-equations-slr,
and give each observation a covariate vector
with a leading 1 for the intercept:

$$
\vxi \eqdef \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ x_i \end{pmatrix}.
$$

Each point on the line is then a dot product,
$\intcoef + \coef{x} x_i = \dprod{\vxi}{\vcoef}$,
so the residual sum of squares is a function of $\vcoef$:

$$
\text{RSS}(\vcoef) = \sumin \paren{y_i - \dprod{\vxi}{\vcoef}}^2.
$$
